question: The mock has a Describe specs button that writes a spec paragraph for you. What should it do in the first release?
context: Today there is nothing behind that button. We need to decide what a user gets when they want their measurements out of the app.

options.label: Copy as text only, no button
options.summary: You measure, then copy a clean text list of every measurement to paste into a bug, doc, or chat. The written-for-you spec comes later.
pros: Predictable and instant, works everywhere text works
cons: The delightful write it for me moment from the mock is deferred
options.mitigation: The copied list is formatted well enough to paste as a spec with minimal editing.

options.label: Copy as text, plus let other tools ask for it
options.summary: Same copyable list, and other apps or scripts can also request a capture's measurements without opening the app.
pros: Power users and tools can automate their redlining flow
cons: More surface to design and support before the basics have shipped
options.mitigation: Keep the outside interface tiny: one way in, one list out.

options.label: Build the full Describe specs button now
options.summary: One click sends the capture and measurements off and returns a written description of the spec, like the mock promises.
pros: The most magical version of the feature, exactly as mocked
cons: Biggest effort, and it depends on plumbing that does not exist yet, so it would delay everything else
options.mitigation: If chosen, ship it behind a flag so the rest of Measure does not wait on it.
